statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 17% (low), Stress 51% (elevated), Confidence 87% (high), dominant mode trend-up. The 20:00Z cash close printed NASDAQ-100 at 31,076.44, about 41 points under the 31,117.36 session high, and NQZ26 is 31,336.00 at 20:18:29Z, roughly 35 points beneath its 31,370.75 extreme. The power-hour continuation leg flagged an hour ago did not develop.
recommendation: Tail falls three points to 17%, back inside the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON and green for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The prior hour published 20% and named power hour into the 20:00Z cash close as the narrow danger window. That window has now resolved: NQZ26 extended to a marginal new high of 31,370.75, only about 7 points above the extreme named an hour ago, then faded to 31,336.00 and now sits roughly 35 points beneath it rather than the 9 points recorded at 19:17Z. The cash index closed 31,076.44, about 41 points off its own high, and VIX finished 15.54 near its 15.48 session low after a 16.38 high. A retracement that holds into the close is the opposite of the repeated-extension structure that would justify the block threshold. Tail does not fall further than 17% because the advance itself is intact at +0.88% and price remains within roughly 0.1% of an all-time high, so the trend-up regime that produced four record extremes is unresolved rather than reversed. Tail remains well below the block threshold; the narrow evidence-based danger window moves forward to Fed Williams at 13:05Z and the Oct 6 cash open at 13:30Z.
headline: Tail eases to 17% as the power-hour continuation fails to develop: cash closes 31,076.44, about 41 points off its high, and NQ holds 35 points under its 31,370.75 extreme
body:
The prior hour published Tail at 20%, the watch band, and identified power hour into the 20:00Z cash close as the one window where current evidence supported watch-band risk. That window has now passed and the feared structure did not materialise, which is the single most important development of this hour.

NQZ26 did print one further record extreme at 31,370.75, but it exceeded the 31,363.25 high named an hour ago by only about 7 points, and price then faded. The last verified quote is 31,336.00 at 20:18:29Z, up 274.25 points or 0.88% on the 31,061.75 prior close, against a 31,059.00 open and a day range of 30,957.50 to 31,370.75. Price now sits roughly 35 points beneath the extreme, against roughly 9 points at 19:17Z. The cash market confirms the fade: NASDAQ-100 closed at 31,076.44, up 268.51 points or 0.87% on a 30,807.93 prior close, about 41 points under its 31,117.36 session high, having traded a 30,798.42 to 31,117.36 range. An hour earlier the cash index stood at 31,113.02 and about 4 points under that high.

A session that spends the closing hour drifting away from its extreme, rather than being pinned to it, is a retracement that held. For a reverse or grid strategy the pathological case is the opposite: repeated extension after failed pullbacks, with price refusing to give ground into the close. That did not happen, and it is the reason the published value returns from the watch band to the low band.

Volatility confirms the orderly resolution. VIX finished at 15.54, up 1.50% on a 15.31 prior close but near the bottom of its 15.48 to 16.38 session range, so implied volatility decayed as the index set records. Realised magnitude also stayed modest: a 0.87% cash advance across a roughly 1.0% range is an orderly grind rather than violent directional repricing.

Tail eases three points rather than collapsing because the advance itself is intact. The index closed within roughly 0.1% of an all-time high after a session that produced several record extremes, and the trend-up regime is unresolved rather than reversed. Overnight acceptance or rejection of that record close is a genuine open question, which is why the published path holds a 10% to 11% overnight floor instead of returning to the 3% levels seen late on Oct 4.

The amplifier stack remains conflicting rather than aligned, and that continues to cap the published value. Breadth is the clearest constraint: advancing issues led decliners by only 1.04-to-1 on the NYSE and 1.09-to-1 on the Nasdaq beneath a record index level. The Philadelphia semiconductor index fell roughly 0.3% to 0.7% depending on the cut, with Western Digital and Seagate up as much as 6% while the broader chip complex lagged, even as Nvidia gained about 1.1%. The Dow finished the regular session essentially flat to slightly lower on one Reuters-sourced account and modestly higher on another, against a Nasdaq-100 up 0.87%, so participation was narrow in any reading. A record set on near one-to-one breadth with chips lagging is a megacap-led advance, not the broad alignment that produces an index-level one-way path.

Cross-assets conflict in the same direction. The 10-year note yield is reported between 5.296% and 5.34%, with the Federal Reserve H.15 release showing 5.28% for the 10-year and 4.83% for the 2-year as of Oct 2, and the 30-year around 5.70%, described as its highest level since 2002. Crude fell sharply, with WTI at 89.14 dollars down 2.16% and Brent at 100.25 dollars down 1.95%. Equities rising while the long end sells off is a valuation conflict that belongs in Stress, not in Tail. One account framed the dynamic directly: growth stocks are rallying because Fed expectations have softened, while the risk-free rate against which those valuations are judged remains exceptionally high.

Composition reinforces the point. A material share of the Oct 5 move was idiosyncratic deal flow rather than index structure: PTC rose about 34.6% on Schneider Electric's 22.6 billion dollar acquisition, RXO gained about 22.5% on a 5.8 billion dollar C.H. Robinson agreement, and Cerebras Systems added about 9.5% after being named a close partner by OpenAI. Single-stock merger and partnership moves do not create a one-way index path.

The macro backdrop is identifiable. September ISM Services printed 54.9% at 14:00Z, a 0.5 point decrease from August's 55.4% and the 27th consecutive month of expansion, with Business Activity at 56.5%, New Orders at 59.8%, Employment back in expansion at 50.1% and Prices at 74.0%. Hot services prices alongside a soft Sep payroll print of 29,000 explain why the long end has stayed firm even as October rate-hike expectations receded. Stress therefore eases only three points to 51% and stays in the elevated band.

The narrow evidence-based danger window moves forward to 13:00Z to 15:00Z on Oct 6, covering Fed Williams at 13:05Z, the 13:30Z cash open and Fed Bowman at 14:45Z. An opening auction that continues from a record close with shallow pullbacks is the specific structure that would justify the watch band, and it is where the published path peaks at 17%. Every slot of the 24 modelled stays inside the low band, and every forward value is conditional risk rather than observed structure.

The shared Finviz context file was read and not used. Its generatedAt is 2026-09-29T23:14:22Z, roughly six days old, and its collectionStatus is partial, so it falls far outside the 90-minute freshness bound and cannot support current cross-asset evidence. Every level cited above was fetched independently from primary and reputable current sources instead, which is why Confidence holds at 87% despite the unavailable shared feed.

lookbackSummary: Across the 24 hours to 19:00Z, Claude published Tail between 3% and 20% and Stress between 46% and 71%. Twenty-three of the 24 hours mapped to EA_ON and green; the final slot, 19:00Z, reached 20% and was the single WATCH and yellow hour as NQ pinned itself within about 9 points of a fourth record extreme into power hour. Tail sat at 3% through the Oct 4 US evening, rose into a 12% to 15% overnight band, troughed at 6% during the European morning, then climbed in steps through the US session from 7% at midday to 17%, 18%, 19% and finally 20% as successive session highs were tested, rejected and then exceeded. Stress fell steadily from 71% late on Oct 4 to 46% by midday Oct 5 before firming back to 54% as the long end pressed to multi-decade highs. Dominant mode was normal overnight, briefly trend-down at 10:00Z, mixed through most of the US morning, and trend-up at 14:00Z and again from 17:00Z onward. One hour, 06:00Z on Oct 5, has no published assessment and is marked unavailable rather than filled in.
outlookSummary: The published path treats the Oct 6 US cash open, not the Oct 5 close, as the next window where risk could reach the watch band. Tail opens at 17% for the 20:00Z hour, three points below the prior publication because the power-hour continuation leg failed to develop and the cash close printed about 41 points off its session high. It then falls through 14% and 12% as index liquidity drains, reaching a 10% overnight floor across the Tokyo and Asian mid-session hours with Stress bottoming at 44%. That floor sits above the 3% levels published late on Oct 4 because the record close itself is unresolved overnight. Risk rebuilds through the European session, with mode shifting to mixed at the 07:00Z European open, then tracks the Oct 6 calendar: 14% across the 12:15Z weekly ADP and 12:30Z balance of trade block, a 17% secondary peak spanning Fed Williams at 13:05Z, the 13:30Z cash open and Fed Bowman at 14:45Z, easing to 14% into the 17:00Z 3-year note auction and 13% afterwards, then 14% into the Oct 6 power hour. Every one of the 24 slots stays inside the low band and maps to EA_ON and green. Forward values are conditional risk, not an assertion that any future price path has been observed.
